passage:
A man's smart watch warned him that his heartbeat was unusual. He felt fine, but the warning repeated.
He visited a doctor and learned that the watch had found a problem early. His family was grateful.
In health class, students discussed wearable devices. They can help people notice health changes, but they can also cause worry or give false alarms.
The teacher said devices provide information, not final answers. Doctors, symptoms, and tests still matter.
The smart watch was useful because the man responded wisely. Technology can notice signals, but humans must decide what action to take.
